title: Making room for a different rest
meaning: Leaving an old activity behind can make room for pleasure if the search for quiet leaves you available to each other.
text: Sometimes leisure changes through a clear “We don't enjoy this any more”. Death in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes ending an old activity so another pleasure has room. The Hermit in energy leans towards withdrawing into private quiet here: a shared wish becomes harder to hear when each person retreats in advance. The Emperor in emotions seeks security in clear boundaries, the comfort of knowing which activity you will no longer have to endure. Removing something unwanted still leaves shared enjoyment to be created.

Suppose you stop attending a regular noisy event. The free evening finally belongs to you, yet each person takes a separate corner and waits for a new kind of rest to happen. **Freed time becomes shared through a living invitation.** A small suggestion to make an unusual drink or listen to a few songs can begin the evening without immediately establishing another compulsory tradition that fills all the available time.

The difficulty is protecting the freed space so strictly that every invitation seems like another intrusion. You wanted to stop enduring an uncomfortable activity and also narrowed the possibility of a pleasant surprise. Quiet is available, while shared enjoyment is scarce. Boundaries serve rest when they leave room within them for freely agreeing to something small and new.
